name: BÁCIGA
description: Báciga is the distinct Uruguayan evolution of the Spanish fishing game 'Escoba'. While it retains the core mechanic of capturing cards that sum to 15, Báciga adds a layer of 'declarations' (hand combinations) similar to Poker or Rummy. Points are scored through table captures, 'Escobas' (clearing the table), and special three-card combos like the 'Chorizo'. It is widely celebrated in Uruguay as a faster, more combo-driven alternative to Truco.

content.text: Báciga is the distinct Uruguayan evolution of the Spanish fishing game 'Escoba'. While it retains the core mechanic of capturing cards that sum to 15, Báciga adds a layer of 'declarations' (hand combinations) similar to Poker or Rummy. Points are scored through table captures, 'Escobas' (clearing the table), and special three-card combos like the 'Chorizo'. It is widely celebrated in Uruguay as a faster, more combo-driven alternative to Truco.
Derived from the Spanish game 'Escoba de 15' which was brought to South America by immigrants. In Uruguay, it merged with elements of the game 'Chorizo' to become the modern Báciga.
2-4 players. 4-player games are usually partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
Standard Spanish deck, pen and paper for 21-point tracking.
1. Dealer deals 3 cards to each player face down. 2. 4 cards are dealt face up to the table. 3. Dealing is counter-clockwise.

items.text: Chorizo (Traditional): The 'parent' game where the declaration values are much higher and the session usually goes to 31 points.
